tutorial: No FreeCAD wiki tutorial covers Texturizer (an add-on). The part is the wiki's Part_Box.md primitive, 40 x 30 x 10 mm, textured as BumpMesh's own workflow goes (README.md of Texturizer-FreeCAD; guide_read { topic: "texture" }): one-call apply on the top face, then the draft with two layers, preview, apply, check, export, a CAD change and Update.

conventions.placeholders: None: every call names its objects by label (Grip, Grip_hex, Grip_textured), so the calls do not depend on earlier answers. Run in order; chunks of 20 may be cut anywhere.
conventions.faces: A Part box: Face1 x=0, Face2 x=40, Face3 y=0, Face4 y=30, Face5 z=0 (bottom), Face6 z=10 (top).
conventions.refused: An expect starting REFUSED means the call must answer isError with that code; nothing in the document changes.
conventions.measuredHere: The numbers marked as the plain-Python engine's were run on this box as 12 triangles outside FreeCAD (texturizer.engine): estimates are exact; triangle counts after decimation and repair may differ a little with FreeCAD's tessellation order.

oneCallApply.seconds: about 4 in plain Python on the build machine

afterHeight12.Grip_textured: reruns by itself (TextureState updating… then up to date)

notCovered: texture_draft { project: "ask" }, texture_set { texture: { upload: true } }, stamp: "place", frame { face: "selected" }, texture_mask { add: "selected" }, texture_export without path: each waits for a person at the window (a dialog or a pick)
texture_set frame / cylinder / stamp { point, normal }: a box has no cylinder to fit; add a part_primitive cylinder and texture_set { cylinder: "autofit" } by hand to cover them
texture_apply { bake: true }: makes the result the draft's part; left out to keep the model's later calls independent
texture_preview { turntable: true } (a running spin) and the background rerun's timing: watch by eye
A Mesh part (triangles, fill { triangles }): needs an imported STL
